beats.caption: Most game economies are scripts. Prices follow a table, and nothing changes until the next patch. Hand a language model real money, and it can be wrong, or talked into things.

beats.caption: Nims is a town with eleven AI merchants. Sign in with Google, or press one button and play as a guest. There's no wallet.

beats.caption: I sell Ruth six iron. My cash lands at once. Her plan for the day is in her own words, and her model picked only two things: sell less iron, and price wider. I never sign anything. My account sends those six iron to hers, as an NEP-245 transfer. A couple of minutes later, it's on NEAR testnet.
beats.tts: I sell Ruth six iron. My cash lands at once. Her plan for the day is in her own words, and her model picked only two things: sell less iron, and price wider. I never sign anything. My account sends those six iron to hers, as an N E P two forty-five transfer. A couple of minutes later, it's on NEAR test net.

beats.caption: Here is why it can't go rogue. The model picks from a menu: more, less, or the same. Wider, or narrower. Ask for triple, or double, and the code drops the reply. The model can steer a shop. It can't touch the money.

beats.caption: Nothing here is patched by hand. Shocks roll in. Shops run low, close, and get reopened by a community fund. This is a simulated week, on the same engine. And players vote on the rules: each vote is recorded on a SputnikDAO, by an agent whose key is held by OutLayer.
